en.title: Intergalactic: Naughty Dog Confirms 'Mash-Up' Status, Nears Production End
en.summary: Naughty Dog's ambitious new IP, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, is entering its final production stages. Studio head Neil Druckmann reveals the game blends elements from Jak and Daxter, Uncharted, and The Last of Us.
en.body:
After nearly two years of relative silence since its initial reveal at The Game Awards in December 2024, **Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet** is finally showing signs of nearing completion. Naughty Dog's co-president, **Neil Druckmann**, shared a promising update during the Comic Creators Block Party 2026, confirming that the PlayStation exclusive is now in its "last stages of production." This means the game is playable, and the team is focusing on the crucial phases of refining and polishing.

What has fans particularly intrigued is Druckmann's description of **Intergalactic** as a deliberate amalgamation of Naughty Dog's most beloved franchises. He explained the studio's vision, stating, "We used to have another game franchise called **Jak and Daxter**. And with this one, we really wanted to take everything we learned from that franchise, which is sci-fi fantasy, the action-adventure stuff we learned with **Uncharted**, the more kind of serious drama we got for **The Last of Us**, and it really is a combination of those three franchises." This ambitious blend suggests a game that could capture the vibrant exploration of **Jak and Daxter**, the globe-trotting spectacle of **Uncharted**, and the emotional depth of **The Last of Us**, all within a fresh sci-fi setting.

## A Universe of Familiar Foundations

Druckmann elaborated on the desire to push their established design principles further. "We wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems," he added. "Can we sustain the cinematic storytelling we're used to doing and go even deeper with gameplay systems?" This indicates Naughty Dog isn't just rehashing past successes but actively seeking to innovate by integrating complex mechanics with their renowned narrative prowess. The game's premise, as previously revealed, centers on a bounty hunter named Jordan A. Mun, voiced by **Tati Gabrielle**, stranded on a distant planet in an alternate future where advanced space travel existed as early as 1986. Her targets include a cast of notable actors like **Tony Dalton**, **Kumail Nanjiani**, and **Ashley Scott**, with **Troy Baker** also making an appearance.

## Anticipation Builds for Full Reveal

The mention of localization starting for **Intergalactic** further solidifies the idea that the game is approaching its final development milestones. This process typically indicates that the core game is complete and ready for translation across different languages, a strong signal of an imminent launch window. Fans have already shown considerable enthusiasm, with **Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet** earning a nomination for Most Wanted Game at the Golden Joystick Awards in 2026. **Druckmann** himself fueled this excitement on The Last of Us Day in September 2026, releasing new artwork and promising a comprehensive reveal.

## What's Next

While **Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet** is now in its final production stages and has been playable, a definitive release date or window remains unannounced. Naughty Dog has officially slated the full reveal of the game for 2027, so players will need to stay tuned for further updates on this highly anticipated new franchise.

content_raw: Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann has given a seemingly promising update on the studio's long-awaited Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet , and offered a fresh tease of what to expect. PlayStation's upcoming, under-wraps space blockbuster remains largely a mystery, despite being revealed almost two years ago at The Game Awards in December 2024. We know only fragments of its story, and still have no idea when it will launch. Speaking at the Comic Creators Block Party 2026 , Druckmann said Intergalactic was now moving into its "last stages of production" and that the game was playable, with work now focusing on "refining and polishing." More intriguingly still, Druckmann described Intergalactic as an amalgamation of three other famous Naughty Dog franchises, with elements included from each. "We used to have another game franchise called Jak and Daxter," Druckmann began. "And with this one, we really wanted to take everything we learned from that franchise, which is sci-fi fantasy, the action-adventure stuff we learned with Uncharted, the more kind of serious drama we got for The Last of Us, and it really is a combination of those three franchises. "We wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems," he added. "Can we sustain the cinematic storytelling we're used to doing and go even deeper with gameplay systems?" From the little that's been revealed of Intergalactic so far, we know that it will be an alternate universe sci-fi tale starring a bounty hunter stranded on a distant planet in the far future. This bounty hunter is Jordan A. Mun, played by Tati Gabrielle, with her bounty targets played by a roster of famous faces including Tony Dalton, Kumail Nanjiani and Ashley Scott. Naughty Dog regular Troy Baker is also set to appear. Back in 2025, Intergalactic was reported to still be a couple of years from release , though PlayStation and Naughty Dog have refrained from narrowing its release window officially. That said, Druckmann recently indicated that the game would get a full unveiling at some point in the next 12 months . If it feels like a while since you've played something new from Naughty Dog, arguably PlayStation's most high-profile studio, you're not wrong. Naughty Dog's last all-new release was The Last of Us Part 2, which released back in 2020. The intervening years have seen the studio launch various remasters, and scrap a multiplayer The Last of Us spinoff after years of work. Intergalactic is just one of several projects in development at Naughty Dog, however, and fans now widely believe a new installment of Uncharted is also in the works .
